title: Distinct Points with a Record
oneLiner: Turn a plain Point class into a record (or frozen dataclass) so equal points really are equal, then remove duplicates with a set.
keyTakeaway: A hash set can only spot duplicates if equal objects compare equal and hash equally. A record or a frozen dataclass gives you both from the field list; a plain class compares by identity, so two Point(1, 2) objects are different and nothing is ever a duplicate.
explanation:
The starter code has an ordinary Point class with X and Y, and a Distinct(points) method to finish: return the points with duplicates removed, keeping the first occurrence of each, in order. [(1, 2), (1, 2), (3, 4)] gives [(1, 2), (3, 4)].

Write the loop with a HashSet<Point> (C#) or a set (Python): for each point, if it isn't in the set, add it to the set and to the result. Then run the tests: they still fail, because the plain class compares by identity, so every Point is different from every other, even with the same X and Y. The fix is the point of the exercise: make Point a record, public record Point(int X, int Y);, or in Python a @dataclass(frozen=True) with fields x and y. Both generate equality and a matching hash code. (Plain @dataclass isn't enough in Python: without frozen=True it has no hash, so it can't go in a set.)

Each test also checks Point itself: the last value in the result is true only if Point(0, 0) equals Point(0, 0) and a set of two such points has just one item. The points are shown as [x, y] pairs.

complexity.note: One pass with an O(1) average set lookup per point, thanks to the record's hash code. The set and the result hold up to n points. Checking the result list instead of a set would be O(n²).
